{{2024–25 MEAC men's basketball standings}}
The '''2024–25 North Carolina Central Eagles men's basketball team''' represented [[North Carolina Central University]] during the [[2024–25 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Eagles, led by 16th-year head coach [[LeVelle Moton]], played their home games at [[McDougald–McLendon Arena]] in [[Durham, North Carolina]] as members of the [[Mid-Eastern Athletic Conference]].

==Previous season==
The [[2023–24 North Carolina Central Eagles men's basketball team|Eagles]] finished the [[2023–24 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2023–24 season]] 18–13, 9–5 in MEAC play to finish in a three-way tie for second place.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://meacsports.com/standings.aspx?standings=61|title=2023-24 Men's Basketball Standings|work=[[Mid-Eastern Athletic Conference]]|access-date=November 21, 2024|language=en}}</ref> They defeated [[2023–24 Maryland Eastern Shore Hawks men's basketball team|Maryland Eastern Shore]],<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/cleveland-scores-21-north-carolina-central-beats-maryland-eastern-shore-87-81-in-meac-tournament/|title=Cleveland scores 21, North Carolina Central beats Maryland-Eastern Shore 87-81 in MEAC Tournament|work=[[CBS Sports]]|access-date=November 21, 2024|language=en}}</ref> before being upset by [[2023–24 Delaware State Hornets men's basketball team|Delaware State]] in the semifinals of the [[2024 MEAC men's basketball tournament|MEAC tournament]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://apnews.com/sports/college-basketball-mens-college-basketball-norfolk-487baec16c68405b90a417c87dec02dc|title=Delaware State upsets second-seeded North Carolina Central 71-58 in MEAC semifinal|work=[[Associated Press|AP News]]|access-date=November 21, 2024|language=en}}</ref>
